product_brief: A SASE platform providing quantum-ready security, hybrid PQC negotiation, and compliance with FIPS 140-3 and NIAP standards.
pqc_capability_description: Versa integrates X25519Kyber768 hybrid key exchange. It dynamically adapts to PQC negotiations: if the server rejects it, VOS re-negotiates; if accepted and TLS decryption is not enabled, it forwards the session; if decryption is not yet supported for the hybrid mechanism, it negotiates a compatible non-Kyber alternative to preserve connectivity.
key_management_model: Hybrid key exchange methods (X25519Kyber768); dynamic negotiation of ciphers via VOS.
architecture_type: SASE platform, TLS proxy, firewall, security proxy
fips_validated: Yes (FIPS 140-3 compliant; mentions support for FIPS-compliant PQC functions)
primary_platforms: VOS (Versa Operating System), Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (mentioned as supporting FIPS-compliant PQC functions)
regulatory_status: FIPS 140-3, NIAP validation, DoD encryption requirements
pqc_roadmap_details: Gradual adoption of hybrid PQC algorithms (X25519Kyber768) to maintain backward compatibility while preparing for full PQC adoption; phasing out legacy cryptographic algorithms.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports gradual adoption and hybrid environments to prevent disruptions; ensures operational continuity without compromising existing security frameworks.

product_brief: A cloud security platform currently in development for quantum-resilient encryption using NIST PQC algorithms.
pqc_capability_description: Quantum-resilient Netskope One is currently in development. It focuses on NIST’s PQC algorithms, specifically ML-KEM 768, to build greater protections across infrastructure. It is intended to be available for sandbox testing by customers shortly, providing full existing platform functionality based on NIST recommendations.
pqc_roadmap_details: Focusing on NIST’s PQC algorithms (specifically ML-KEM 768). Quantum-resilient Netskope One is currently in development and intended to be available for sandbox testing by customers shortly.

product_brief: Quantum-ready Security Service Edge (SSE) providing inline inspection and hybrid PQC key exchange for TLS and IPsec.
pqc_capability_description: Supports hybrid PQC key exchange for TLS 1.3 using NIST-standardized ML-KEM (FIPS 203) compliant with draft-ietf-tls-echde-mlkem. Enables inline decryption/inspection of PQC traffic. Supports IPsec VPNs with Post-quantum Pre-shared Keys (PPK) mixed into IKE key derivation. Protects against HNDL attacks.
crypto_primitives: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), TLS 1.3, Diffie-Hellman with Ephemeral keys (DHE/ECDHE), Post-quantum Pre-shared Keys (PPK)
key_management_model: Hybrid PQC key exchange for TLS; Post-quantum Pre-shared Keys (PPK) mixed into IKE key derivation for IPsec
pqc_roadmap_details: Current support for hybrid PQC key exchange (ML-KEM) and PPK for IPsec; focus on crypto-agility and visibility.
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Yes (real-time crypto inventory capabilities, detailed reporting on quantum cipher usage, visibility into PQC support on client side)
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Low (applies existing security policies without configuration changes; independent of server capabilities)
